mechanics.name: Red Herring
mechanics.currentEffect: After repairing a Generator for at least 1 second, its Aura is highlighted yellow to you. The highlight ends if the Generator is completed, you start repairing another Generator, or you enter a Locker. Entering a Locker while a Generator is highlighted causes a Loud Noise Notification for the Killer at that Generator. Red Herring then has a 25/20/15-second cooldown by tier.
activation: Repair a Generator for at least 1 second to highlight it.
Enter a Locker while the Generator is highlighted to trigger the Loud Noise Notification.
Ends/deactivates when: The Generator's Aura highlight ends if the Generator is completed, you begin repairing another Generator, or you enter a Locker.
Ends/deactivates when: The cooldown prevents another activation until it expires.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (8.6.0): Reduced the repair requirement from 3 seconds to 1 second and reduced cooldown to 25/20/15 seconds from 30/25/20.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: Repair a Generator briefly to mark it, then entering a Locker sends the Killer a Loud Noise Notification at the marked Generator.
duration: Generator Aura highlight: until the Generator is completed, you start repairing a different Generator, or you enter a Locker.
specialInteractions: The Killer receives a Loud Noise Notification at the highlighted Generator when you enter a Locker; the notification does not reveal your Aura.

editorial.summary: Briefly repair a Generator to mark it, then enter a Locker to send the Killer a fake Loud Noise notification at that Generator.
useCases: Fake a missed Skill Check on a Generator far from the team’s real pressure.
Pair with a Locker perk so the activation is not a pure detour.
Try to pull a high-mobility Killer toward an irrelevant objective after they finish another task.
counters: The Killer may ignore the notification or recognize the bait.
Activating requires leaving productive work and entering a Locker.
A fake notification on an important Generator may accidentally encourage the Killer to defend it.
pros: Can create a remote notification at a chosen Generator.
cons: Can actively attract the Killer to a Generator you care about.
analysis: Red Herring offers a remote fake notification, which sounds strategically flexible until the cost is counted. You must first mark a Generator, leave it, find a Locker, and trust the Killer to believe the resulting noise matters.

The best-case use is sending a mobile Killer toward a generator that is strategically irrelevant while the team pressures elsewhere. That requires timing, map awareness, and an opponent willing to react.
The downside is comical when the marked generator is actually important. A successful bait can bring the Killer directly to progress the team hoped to preserve.
Red Herring remains near the bottom because every layer of value depends on the Killer making the mistake you hoped for. It can be hilarious and still be bad.
editorial.verdict: A remote decoy with too many chores and too much opponent agency. Red Herring is a fun lie that often costs more time to tell than the Killer loses believing it.
